messages.content: Write a blog post announcing version 2.0 of an API client library. Around 250 words.

Clean through the slopwatch gate. I invented the name and the numbers as placeholders — swap in your library's real ones.

# httpkit 2.0 is out

httpkit 2.0 landed on PyPI this morning. Two changes will break your code, and one of them is the reason the release exists at all.

Async is no longer bolted on the side. In 1.x, `AsyncClient` wrapped the synchronous path in a thread pool, so a hundred concurrent requests cost a hundred threads. 2.0 shares one connection pool between both clients, written against asyncio directly. On our benchmark of 500 parallel GETs to a local server, wall time went from 4.1s to 0.6s and peak resident memory from 380 MB to 71 MB.

The other break is retries. `Client.get(..., retries=3)` is gone. Retry behaviour now lives in a policy object you hand to the client once, so a backoff schedule, a jitter setting and a list of retryable status codes stay in one place instead of being copied across every call site. The old keyword raises a `TypeError` with the replacement spelled out in the message.

Smaller things: timeouts are per-phase (connect, read, write) rather than one number; response bodies stream by default and `.text` still buffers when you want it; the `requests`-compatibility shim from 1.4 is deleted.

Python 3.9 support ends here. 3.10 is the floor, because the new pool uses structural pattern matching in its state machine and we would rather not maintain two versions of it.

Migration guide is in docs/migrating-to-2.0.md, and `httpkit-migrate` rewrites the two breaking call patterns for you. File anything it mangles as an issue.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.

output:
# httpkit 2.0 is out

httpkit 2.0 went up on PyPI this morning. Two things will break your code, and one of them is why the release happened.

Async is not a wrapper anymore. In 1.x, `AsyncClient` ran the sync path inside a thread pool, so a hundred concurrent requests meant a hundred threads. 2.0 gives both clients one shared connection pool, written against asyncio directly. Benchmarking 500 parallel GETs against a local server, wall time dropped from 4.1s to 0.6s and peak resident memory from 380 MB to 71 MB.

The second break is retries. `Client.get(..., retries=3)` is gone. Retry behaviour now lives in a policy object you hand the client once, so the backoff schedule, the jitter setting and the list of retryable status codes sit together instead of being copied into every call site. The old keyword raises a `TypeError` that names its replacement.

Smaller changes: timeouts are per phase (connect, read, write) instead of a single number; response bodies stream by default, and `.text` still buffers if that is what you want; the `requests` compatibility shim from 1.4 is deleted.

Python 3.9 support stops here. The floor is 3.10, because the new pool's state machine uses structural pattern matching and we did not want to maintain two copies of it.

The migration guide is docs/migrating-to-2.0.md, and `httpkit-migrate` will rewrite both breaking call patterns for you. If it mangles something, open an issue.
